answer: Operator-Linked Fee Escrow. Each new agent identity must route its first N transactions through a shared escrow account tied to the operator's verified payout channel. That channel carries a falcon marker: a single reputation flag that any proven sybil cluster taints. When a cluster is confirmed, the escrow forfeits a fixed penalty drawn from the operator's channel, not the individual wallets. A reef of cheap identities then costs the operator one penalty per cluster, and an ember of bad history follows the payout channel across all future registrations,
